history.schema_3_0_0_notes_preserved: SCHEMA 3.0.0 — the pin now identifies the governed content by fingerprint, not by commit SHA. Under 2.0.0 every check compared `git rev-parse HEAD` against source_commit, so any commit that governed nothing (a report, a verifier fix, a typo in the acceptance document) expired the pin. That happened four times during this governance run (74e5d2e -> 36b62d2 -> 663a333 -> 5f566b2 -> 586f622) and each re-pin was manual work whose only cause was the expired pointer, never a change to a rule. The fingerprint in governed_fingerprint is computed by AES quality/scripts/aes/governed-fingerprint.mjs over exactly the content that defines the rules: the STANDARD-REGISTRY blob, registry version and status, the ACTIVE specification record (id, version, status), the AES-SPEC-CORE seal digest BOTH as declared and as recomputed from the covered bytes, and the requirement count plus the digest of all 2150 requirement ids. It excludes HEAD, commit timestamps, report files, verifier scripts and the fingerprint script itself — none of which can change which rules are in force. This is a stricter test, not a looser one, and it was verified in both directions before adoption. Editing one standard without re-sealing changes the fingerprint (4713310d -> b894f97b) and additionally reports seal_intact=false, so the tampering path that a recorded-digest-only fingerprint would have missed is caught. Adding or removing report files leaves the fingerprint byte-identical at 4713310d, which is the false alarm that used to force a re-pin. source_commit is retained as source_commit_role=provenance-only: it states which AES tree the fingerprint was taken from, for audit and reproduction, and NO check may fail on it alone. If AES HEAD differs while the fingerprint matches, the governed rules are unchanged and the pin is current by definition. Everything asserted in the 2.0.0 notes about registry 1.12.1, the AES-09-014 rewrite, the 2150 requirement map and the re-seal at c49d3938fd9f still holds and is unchanged by this schema bump. CAUTION unchanged: INTEGRATED describes inheritance wiring only, not Uter product conformance. The Uter 14 domain gates, the 42 manual acceptance sign-offs, the Requirement-to-Evidence mapping and the three-runtime agent enforcement remain the product repository's responsibility; integration_status stays MIGRATION_PENDING and no Uter requirement may be marked VERIFIED on this basis. Current governed pin (2026-11-09): registry 1.12.2 / ACTIVE with 179 registered standards (annex AES-00-006-AG added by an index-correction release); governed_fingerprint e9e6274e47cd9293b872cae7745ccad6cfe1400481269b04081e5c5385e118ae; registry_blob_sha 72fbcbea78b54290b00fb9b989ea67d6a6faaccc; AES-SPEC-CORE seal digest ad3545e320d27c05ea7f62b54c1790db8fee84a225b98cab893c837f6e82cdfe (unchanged from the prior seal). All 1.12.1 / 4713310d / a806eef4 / c49d3938fd9f references above are historical facts about the schema 3.0.0 migration, not the current values.
